title: Flight Deck Shift Handoff & Hotfix Breadcrumbs
content:
Context: Weekly Friday handoff for Release Engineering's 'flight deck' rotation. This doc captures the 2026-03-09 17:00 PST sync, outstanding hotfix breadcrumbs, and the decisions we made for next week

Attendees:
- Rina Patel (owner)
- Theo Marshall (release lead)
- Jin Soo Park (SRE)
- Maya Gomez (release engineer - deploys)
- Owen Blake (QA lead)
- Notes: few join-lates, recording in release-flight-deck slack thread

Agenda (5 items):
1) Quick status: active trains, blocked PRs, capacity headroom
2) Hotfix queue triage (blocking and P1s)
3) Canary and telemetry anomalies from this morning's push
4) Rollout gating/rollback readiness for next week's Dedicated deploys
5) Shift handoffs and on-call coverage for weekend window

Summary of current trains:
- Train Alpha (v1.14.2): on track, canary healthy after yesterday's patch. Target stable window Mon 03/15 01:00-03:00 UTC.
- Train Bravo (internal infra): delayed due to infra-1268 (kube-probe race). Waiting on PR #7193 for probe backoff.
- Quickfix stream: two hotfixes pending verification (HF-93, HF-94). HF-92 closed after rollback validation.

Hotfix queue triage (decisions & breadcrumbs):
- HF-93 (embed-cache eviction regression): Priority P0 for customer-facing inference failures. Action: Jin to root cause memory leak in kv-cache and prepare a revert-ready patch by Sun 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC. If patch not ready, execute emergency rollback per rollback playbook.
- HF-94 (console auth 2FA flow edge-case): Priority P1. Maya to coordinate test harness and merge small fix; expected deploy Mon 03/15 during low-traffic window.
- Blocker HF candidate (proxy TLS handshake intermittent): flagged but lower repro rate; add to next triage if occurrence >3 in 24h.

Canary & telemetry notes from 2026-03-09 morning deploy:
- Canary ran 2.5 hours. Error budget consumption 0.6% — within threshold. Observed 1.2x tail latency increase at 95th percentile for model gptx-7b-quant under longer sequences (>1024 tokens).
- Jin traced increased tail latency to suboptimal kernel selection triggered by new cudnn minor update on infra nodes. Temporary mitigation: pin driver on canary workers and trigger re-eval by infra team.
- Decision: pause further gptx-7b-quant rollouts until kernel regression tests added to CI pipeline (owner: Theo).

Rollout gating / rollback readiness:
- For all Dedicated pool deploys next week, require: canary healthy for 3 continuous hours, latency delta < 10% for 95p, and successful synthetic prompt regression checks.
- Rollback checklist review: Maya updated runbook to include KV cache flush command and step-by-step internal notification template (PR attached: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7193).
- Emergency rollback owner escalation matrix reviewed; Rina on-call Sat 03/14 08:00-20:00 PST (primary), Owen backup.

CI / Release automation items:
- Flaky test surge: integration::session-rehydration failing intermittently (3/10 runs). Owen to triage with test owners, mark as flaky and add targeted retries in CI for the short term.
- Release pipeline optimization idea: split large docker build stage into model-artifact and infra image layers to reduce rebuild time. Theo to prototype; target improvement: 20% faster warm builds.

Action items (owner — due):
- Jin Soo Park — root cause and patch for HF-93, prepare revert-ready PR (due 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC)
- Maya Gomez — prepare HF-94 test harness, schedule low-traffic deploy (due 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC)
- Theo Marshall — add kernel selection regression test to CI and prototype docker layer split (initial notes due 2026-03-16)
- Owen Blake — triage session-rehydration flakiness and add short-term CI retries (due 2026-03-13 23:59 UTC)
- Rina Patel — confirm weekend on-call rota and publish updated handoff template to slack (done by 2026-03-11)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: memory leak in kv-cache causing gradual OOMs in long-lived worker pools. Mitigation: emergency OCI image with patched allocator, canary pin, increased monitoring for OOM kill signals.
- Risk: kernel regression causing 95p latency spikes for quantized workloads. Mitigation: pin drivers on canary, add synthetic workloads to nightly CI, hold gptx-7b-quant rollout.

Follow-ups / open questions:
- Should we broaden the emergency rollback policy to include automatic fallback to model-variant with smaller memory footprint? (Action: product + research to evaluate by 2026-03-20)
- Ask infra: can we add a driver-version label to nodes so routing can avoid problem drivers? (Jira: INFRA-3349)

Notes to next shift (hand-off):
- HF-93 remains hottest item — assume on-call will coordinate rollback if HF patch not merged by Sun noon.
- Canary metrics channel configured: #canary-metrics-alerts. If error budget usage >1% within 1 hour, escalate to Rina + Jin immediately.
- Deployments: postpone non-critical Dedicated deploys until kernel regression tests land in CI.

Appendix (quick refs):
- Recent changelog snippets: commit a1b2c3d — patch for session token expiry; commit d4e5f6a — probe backoff tweak.
- Useful links: Jira board: https://jira.redwood/boards/release-engineering | Playbook: confluence.redwood/release/playbooks/rollback

End of notes. Next touchpoint: Mon 2026-03-15 09:30 PST (standup focused on HF progress and canary re-eval).
